2027-05-18.title: Tuesday of the Seventh Week in Ordinary Time · St John I
readings: My child, when you come to serve the Lord, prepare yourself for testing
Commit your life to the Lord, and he will help you
Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all
2027-05-18.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 7 (Year I). Ordinary Time resumed on the Monday after Pentecost; the Angelus has again taken the place of the Regina Caeli, and the Paschal candle now stands by the baptismal font. Liturgical colour: green. Optional memorial: St John I, pope and martyr (colour red if his Mass is said). Two days after Pentecost the weekday readings return to the Book of Sirach and to the Gospel of Mark, where they paused before Lent.
2027-05-18.verse: He sat down, called the twelve, and said to them, “Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.”
theo: After the great feasts of Easter and Pentecost, the Church takes us back to the school of daily life, and the teacher she chooses is Jesus ben Sira, a wise man of Jerusalem who wrote about two hundred years before Christ. His first lesson for anyone who wants to belong to God is honest and a little startling: “My child, when you come to serve the Lord, prepare yourself for testing.” Faith is not an insurance policy against trouble. Ben Sira does not promise an easy road; he promises a faithful God. “Set your heart right and be steadfast, and do not be impetuous in time of calamity. Cling to him and do not depart.” Then comes the image that has comforted believers for centuries: “For gold is tested in the fire, and those found acceptable, in the furnace of humiliation.” The goldsmith does not put gold in the fire to destroy it but to make it pure. Three times the reading repeats “You who fear the Lord”: wait for his mercy, trust in him, hope for good things. And it ends with a challenge to look at history: “Consider the generations of old and see: has anyone trusted in the Lord and been disappointed?” The answer the whole Bible gives is no, “for the Lord is compassionate and merciful; he forgives sins and saves in time of distress.” The Psalm adds its counsel: “Trust in the Lord, and do good.”

In the Gospel Jesus is walking through Galilee, quietly, “for he was teaching his disciples.” For the second time he tells them plainly what lies ahead: “The Son of Man is to be betrayed into human hands, and they will kill him, and three days after being killed, he will rise again.” This is the testing Ben Sira spoke of, and Jesus walks into it first. “But they did not understand what he was saying and were afraid to ask him.” While their Master speaks of the cross, the disciples are busy with another question. At Capernaum he asks them, “What were you arguing about on the way?” Nobody answers, “for on the way they had argued with one another who was the greatest.” Jesus does not scold them. He sits down, as a teacher does, and gives them a new measure of greatness: “Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.” Then he takes a little child, in that world a person with no rank or rights, puts the child in the middle of them, and holds the child in his arms: “Whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me.” Today the Church remembers St John I, an elderly pope who in 526 died in a prison at Ravenna after being sent on a difficult mission by a suspicious king. He did not seek the first place; he accepted the furnace, and was found to be gold.
outline: Ask: when trouble comes, do I take it as a sign that God has left me?
Gold is purified in the fire; God is faithful in the furnace.
The disciples argue about rank while Jesus speaks of the cross.
Point 3 · A child in his arms
To welcome the least is to welcome Christ and the Father.
“Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.”
live: Name one trial you are carrying now and pray each morning this week: Lord, I cling to you; do not let me depart from you.
Serve the one with no rank (Mark 9:35–37)
Do one hidden service today for someone who cannot repay you: a child, a domestic worker, an elderly neighbour.
2027-05-18.prayer: Lord our God, compassionate and merciful, you test your servants as gold is tested in the fire, and you never forsake those who trust in you. Keep our hearts steadfast in every trial. Lord Jesus, you walked to your cross as the servant of all; cure us of the desire to be the greatest, and teach us to welcome the little ones in your name. Through the prayers of St John I, who suffered in prison for the Church, make us faithful to the end. Amen.
altar: At every Mass the Son of Man who was “betrayed into human hands” gives himself into our hands. The One who said “servant of all” is present on the altar as the Lamb offered for all, and he comes to the smallest and least worthy of us in Holy Communion, as he once took a child into his arms.

quick: Ben Sira warns: whoever comes to serve the Lord must prepare for testing; gold is tested in the fire.
Jesus foretells his Passion and Resurrection a second time; the disciples argue about who is the greatest.
He sets a child among them: to be first, be last and servant of all; whoever welcomes a child welcomes him.
2027-05-18.action: Do one hidden act of service today for someone who has no power to repay you.
2027-05-18.question: In the trials of my life, am I clinging to the Lord or quietly drifting away?
kidsaint: John was an old and gentle pope in Rome about fifteen hundred years ago. A powerful king sent him on a long sea journey to the emperor in Constantinople. The emperor welcomed him with great honour, but when John came back, the king did not trust him and put him in prison, where he died. Lesson: being faithful to Jesus matters more than being important or comfortable.

family.explain: On the road the disciples argued about who was the most important. Jesus did not shout at them. He sat down, took a little child in his arms and said: the greatest is the one who serves everybody. In God's family the best place is not the top chair but the place where we help others.
family.intention: We pray for children who are not wanted or cared for, and for families going through a hard time.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our home or school does work that nobody notices? How can we thank or help them this week?”

illus: In a large hospital in Thrissur, a senior nurse with thirty years of service used to arrive early on her last day of each month and clean the sluice room herself before the junior staff came in. A young nurse once asked her why someone of her rank did the dirtiest job. She smiled: when I was new, I thought being in charge meant giving orders. Then I watched our Lord wash feet. Since then I have never been ashamed of a bucket.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, servant of all, keep us steadfast in trial and humble in service. Amen.
share: My child, when you come to serve the Lord, prepare yourself for testing (Sirach 2:1). What testing am I facing now, and how is God purifying me in it?
On the way they had argued with one another who was the greatest (Mark 9:34). Where do I compete for first place in family, work or parish?
Whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me (Mark 9:37). Who are the little ones I am being asked to welcome?
pm.resp: Commit your life to the Lord, and he will help you.
interc: For all who are being tested by illness, loss or failure, that they may cling to the Lord and not lose hope.
For the Pope and all bishops, that like St John I they may serve faithfully under pressure.
For Christians imprisoned for their faith.
For children who are neglected, abused or trafficked, and for all who protect them.
For our group, that we may stop measuring ourselves against one another and learn to serve.
pm.close: Father, you are compassionate and merciful, and you save in time of distress. Make us servants of all, after the pattern of your Son, who lives and reigns for ever and ever. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Pentecost is over and the ordinary weeks of the year have begun again. The first word the Church gives us is not a soft one. My child, when you come to serve the Lord, prepare yourself for testing (Sirach 2:1). Some people imagine that once we give our lives to God, everything will go smoothly. Ben Sira, a wise teacher of Jerusalem, says the opposite: get ready.

But he gives us a beautiful picture. Gold is tested in the fire (Sirach 2:5). A goldsmith in Thrissur or Kozhikode heats the gold not to spoil it but to burn away what is not gold. When the fire of trouble comes, God is not destroying us. He is purifying us. And Ben Sira asks: has anyone trusted in the Lord and been disappointed? Look back at your own life, and the lives of your parents. God has never failed those who clung to him.

In the Gospel Jesus tells his disciples for the second time that he will be betrayed, killed and raised. And what are they talking about on the road? Who is the greatest (Mark 9:34). It is almost funny, and it is very human. We do the same: in families, in offices, even in parish committees. Jesus does not shout. He sits down, takes a little child in his arms, and says: whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.

Today we remember St John I, an old pope who was sent on a hard journey, then thrown into prison by a king who did not trust him, where he died. He did not choose the first place. He accepted the fire and was found to be pure gold. Let us ask for his courage: to cling to the Lord in trial, and to spend our lives serving the little ones. Amen.
kids: Children, the disciples once had a big argument: who is the most important? Jesus took a small child, maybe as small as you, held the child in his arms and said: if you want to be first, help everybody. So in God's eyes the most important person is the one who serves. Can you help someone today without being asked?

intro: Theme: “Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.”
Gold tested in the fire, disciples arguing about rank, and a child in the arms of Jesus.

sub: Faith is no insurance against trouble.
Has anyone trusted and been disappointed?
q: For gold is tested in the fire, and those found acceptable, in the furnace of humiliation.
Blessed is anyone who endures temptation. Such a one has stood the test and will receive the crown of life that the Lord has promised to those who love him.
points.apply: Name your present trial before God each morning this week and add: I cling to you, Lord.

q: The greater you are, the more you must humble yourself; so you will find favor in the sight of the Lord.
He sat down, called the twelve, and said to them, “Whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.”
points.apply: In one meeting or family discussion this week, let someone else have the last word and the credit.

sub: Welcome the child, welcome Christ, welcome the Father.
q: But I have calmed and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with its mother; my soul is like the weaned child that is with me.
Whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes not me but the one who sent me.
points.apply: Give real time this week to a child or to someone overlooked: listen, play, teach, or simply sit with them.

concl: The way of the disciple passes through the furnace, but the Lord is compassionate and never forsakes those who cling to him.
Greatness in the Kingdom is measured by service, and the little ones are where Christ waits to be welcomed.
2027-05-18.resolve: Do one hidden service each day this week for someone who cannot repay you.
